title: Points and local rings under local-spectrum base change
statement:
Let $f:T\to X$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $p\in X$ any point. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], let $\mathfrak m_A$ be its maximal ideal, and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ be the canonical local-spectrum morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. Form $T_p=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_XT$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $\pi:T_p\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $h:T_p\to T$. For every $q\in T$ with $f(q)=p$, there is exactly one point $\widetilde q\in T_p$ with $h(\widetilde q)=q$; it satisfies $\pi(\widetilde q)=\mathfrak m_A$, and the induced map of local rings $\mathcal O_{T,q}\to\mathcal O_{T_p,\widetilde q}$ is an isomorphism. If $q$ is closed in $T$, then $\widetilde q$ is closed in $T_p$.
More explicitly, for any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ containing $p$, let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ represent $p$ and $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. For any affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$ containing $q$, let $Q\subset D$ represent $q$. Write $S^{-1}D$ for localization at the image of $S$ in $D$, the ring of fractions with denominators in that image [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $h^{-1}(W)$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}D)$, $\widetilde q$ corresponds to $S^{-1}Q$, and the local-ring isomorphism is
$$D_Q\xrightarrow{\sim}(S^{-1}D)_{S^{-1}Q},\qquad d/e\longmapsto(d/1)/(e/1),$$
with inverse $(d/s)/(e/t)\mapsto dt/(se)$ for $s,t\in S$, $e\notin Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni p$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$ containing $q$, and write $\alpha:R\to D$ for the induced map. The canonical-morphism node identifies $A$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and factors $c$ through $U$. The open-fibre-product node identifies $h^{-1}(W)$, compatibly with both projections, with $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_U W$. By the affine-fibre-product and localization-base-change nodes this is $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}D)$, with $h$ induced by $d\mapsto d/1$. Here and below $S^{-1}D$ means localization at $\alpha(S)$; no injectivity of $\alpha$ is assumed.

The point $q$ is represented by $Q$ with $\alpha^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak p$, since the spectrum map is contraction. Thus $Q\cap\alpha(S)=\varnothing$. The localization-spectrum embedding supplies exactly one prime $P$ of $S^{-1}D$ contracting to $Q$. Explicitly $P=S^{-1}Q$: an element $d/s$ is in $P$ iff $d/1$ is, since $s/1$ is a unit, iff $d\in Q$. Let $\widetilde q$ be this point in $h^{-1}(W)$. Every point of $T_p$ mapping to $q$ belongs to this same open $h^{-1}(W)$; hence uniqueness on the affine chart is global. Under $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S^{-1}D$, $r/s$ belongs to the contraction of $P$ iff $\alpha(r)\in Q$, equivalently $r\in\mathfrak p$. That contraction is $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak m_A$, so $\pi(\widetilde q)=\mathfrak m_A$.

proof.text:
Put $B=S^{-1}D$ and $P=S^{-1}Q$. Every $s\in\alpha(S)$ is outside $Q$, hence invertible in $D_Q$. By the localization universal property the map $D	o D_Q$ extends to $v:B	o D_Q$, $d/s\mapsto d/s$. If $d/s
otin P$, then $d
otin Q$, so its image is a unit of $D_Q$. The same universal property extends $v$ uniquely to $\psi:B_P	o D_Q$. Conversely $D	o B_P$ sends every $e
otin Q$ to a unit, so extends uniquely to $\phi:D_Q	o B_P$, $d/e\mapsto(d/1)/(e/1)$. The composite $\psi\phi$ is the identity by uniqueness for $D_Q$. The composite $\phi\psi$ is the identity first on $B$ by uniqueness for $S^{-1}D$, then on $B_P$ by uniqueness again. Thus these are inverse ring isomorphisms, and the fraction formula gives $\psi((d/s)/(e/t))=(d/s)/(e/t)=dt/(se)$, where $e
otin Q$ and $s,t\in\alpha(S)$.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), applied three times; fraction construction of Tag 00CO

proof.text: The affine-open stalk-localization node identifies $\mathcal O_{T,q}$ with $D_Q$ and $\mathcal O_{T_p,\widetilde q}$ with $B_P$, using the affine open $h^{-1}(W)$ from step 1. Under these identifications the stalk map of $h$ sends the germ of $d\in D$ to the germ of $d/1\in B$: this is the induced stalk map of the sheaf morphism defining $h$, whose map on these chart sections is $d\mapsto d/1$. Uniqueness in the localization universal property therefore identifies that stalk map with $\phi$ from step 3. This proves both that the induced map is an isomorphism and that it has exactly the displayed formulas, rather than merely producing an abstract isomorphism of the two local rings.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), (1),(6), with the definition of morphisms of locally ringed spaces; algebra.tex Tag 00CP

proof.text: If $q$ is closed in $T$, the singleton $\{q\}$ is closed. The underlying map of the scheme morphism $h$ is continuous, so $h^{-1}(\{q\})$ is closed in $T_p$. Step 2 identified this inverse image as precisely $\{\widetilde q\}$. Hence $\widetilde q$ is closed in $T_p$, without any Noetherian, finite-type, separatedness or closedness assumption on $p$.

Step 4 uses the affine-open-stalk node to show that the actual stalk map h^♯ is φ, not just some isomorphism. Step 5 uses continuity and the one-point fibre.
